title: Linear reductivity of group schemes in arbitrary characteristic
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme]. A finite-dimensional rational representation is a homomorphism $G\to\operatorname{GL}(V)$ [def-wf-algebraic-representations]. A $k$-subspace $U\subset V$ is invariant if for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and every $g\in G(A)$, the action of $g$ preserves $U\otimes_k A$ inside $V\otimes_k A$. A simple subrepresentation is a nonzero invariant subspace with no nonzero proper invariant subspace. The group scheme $G$ is linearly reductive if every finite-dimensional rational representation is an internal direct sum of simple subrepresentations. The zero representation is the empty direct sum. No characteristic or connectedness assumption is imposed.
